passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: Valentinus came to Rome in the time of Hyginus; Cerdon, Marcion's predecessor, also came in the time of Hyginus; Marcion himself flourished under Anicetus. All these heretical teachers arose after and post-date the apostolic Church; none can trace their origin to the apostles.

passage.excerpt: Marcion of Pontus succeeded [Cerdo] and developed his doctrine, blaspheming with shameless effrontery Him proclaimed as God by the law and the prophets, declaring Him the author of evils, taking delight in war, infirm of purpose, and contrary to Himself. But Jesus, derived from that father above the God who made the world, came into Judaea in the times of Pontius Pilate, was manifested in the form of a man — abolishing the prophets and the law — but not truly taking flesh. He also mutilated the Gospel according to Luke, removing all that is written respecting the generation of the Lord.

evidence.notes: Irenaeus AH 3.3.4 records Polycarp's encounter with Marcion, attesting Marcionite presence near Smyrna.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: Polycarp was instructed by apostles, conversed with many who had seen Christ, and was appointed bishop of Smyrna by apostles in Asia; Irenaeus saw him in his early youth. Polycarp came to Rome in the time of Anicetus and caused many to turn from heretics to the Church, proclaiming the one truth received from the apostles. He called Marcion the first-born of Satan.
